Executive Summary
On 2025 May 27, Runaway Bay Water Company Limited (RBWC) made an application to the
Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR), for an Annual Price Adjustment Mechanism (ANPAM)
adjustment of 3.62%, to be applied to its base rates and other charges.
The OUR has reviewed and examined RBWC’s application and has set out its findings in this
Determination Notice.
The OUR has no objection to the ANPAM base rate adjustment of 3.62% as proposed by RBWC.
This adjustment is in keeping with the requirements specified in Runaway Bay Water Company
Limited - Water and Sewerage Rates Determination Notice, document number
2021/WAS/001/DET.001, which addresses the application of the Price Adjustment
Mechanism, and its relationship to the National Water Commission’s (NWC’s) Price
Adjustment Mechanism.
No proposal was submitted for an adjustment to the company’s reconnection fee.
The ANPAM rate adjustment is a rebasing of a specific set of indices only and mirrors that of
the NWC. The adjustment is applicable to customers’ 2025 May consumption, which will be
reflected in 2025 June bills.
The new base indices for the Price Adjustment Mechanism (PAM) are as follows:
• Foreign Exchange Rate: J$158.11 to US$1.00
• Consumer Price Index: 141.80
• Electricity Charge: J$50.59/kWh.
The new base indices will remain in effect until the next programmed reset of the ANPAM in
2026 May, or the implementation of new tariffs, whichever is earlier.

1. Introduction
1.1. On 2025 May 27, Runaway Bay Water Company Limited (RBWC) made an application to
the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR) for an Annual Price Adjustment Mechanism
(ANPAM) rate adjustment of 3.62%. The request is consistent with the determinations
made in the Runaway Bay Water Company Limited - Water and Sewerage Rates
Determination Notice, document number 2021/WAS/001/DET.001, issued 2021 April
27 (the “Determination Notice”).
1.2. In the Determination Notice, RBWC was granted approval to retain the PAM component
of its’ rate structure. The aim of the mechanism is to correct for movements in the three
indices namely, the Consumer Price Index (CPI), the Jamaican dollar exchange rate
relative to the United States Dollar (FX) and Electricity Prices (kWh).
1.3. The PAM rate adjustment, which was granted to RBWC, is equivalent to that of the
NWC’s PAM. However, the application has a one-month lag, to that of the NWC’s PAM.
The PAM has a feature where there is a reset of the base rates on the anniversary date
of the Determination Notice. In this case the anniversary date would be that of the
NWC’s Tariff Determination Notice. This annual reset of the PAM is known as the Annual
Price Adjustment Mechanism (ANPAM) rate adjustment.
1.4. The ANPAM allows for an adjustment of base rates by the rolling-in of the cumulative
monthly PAM rate adjustments into the base rates. The main objective of the annual
reset is to minimize the monthly PAM differential adjustment on customers’ bills, which
accounts for the variance between the current and the base values for the three (3) PAM
indices.

2. Legal and Regulatory Framework
2.1. The RBWC is regulated by the Office of Utilities Regulation Act and operates under
the following licences (collectively referred to as the Licences):
• Runaway Bay Water Company Limited Water Supply Licence, 2004
• Runaway Bay Water Company Limited Sewerage Service Licence, 2014
• Runaway Bay Water Company Limited Water Supply and Distribution Licence,
2017
2.2. The role and function of the OUR in the water and sewerage sector is governed by
the provisions of the OUR Act. Section 4(1) (a) of the OUR Act, provides that the OUR
is empowered to “regulate the provision of prescribed utility services by licensees or
specified organizations”. The provision of sewerage services and the supply and
distribution of water are included among the prescribed utility services defined in the
First Schedule of the OUR Act.
2.3. Section 4(4) of the OUR Act expressly authorizes the OUR to determine the rates
charged for the provision of a prescribed utility service. The section reads:
“(4) The Office shall have power to determine, in accordance with the
provisions of this Act, the rates or fares which may be charged in respect of the
provisions of a prescribed utility service.”
2.4. In exercise of its powers to determine rates, the OUR issued the Determination
Notice, which sets out the approved rates and charges for RBWC’s services. The
Determination Notice also makes allowance for an annual price adjustment, where
RBWC’s ANPAM rates are tied to that of the NWC. On 2025 April 28 the Office issued
its decision on the NWC’s application for an ANPAM rate adjustment.
2.5. In keeping with the determination regarding the annual reset of the PAM, RBWC has
now applied for an ANPAM rate adjustment of its base rates.

3. OUR Analysis and Determinations
3.1. The OUR’s review and determination of rates is guided by the principle that rates
should be sufficient to cover prudently incurred costs. In this regard, the monthly and
annual price adjustment mechanisms are designed to align the rates with prudently
incurred input cost.
The Price Adjustment Mechanism
3.2. The PAM allows RBWC to adjust its rates monthly to account for the effect of changes
in input cost that are exogenous to its operations. It therefore seeks to preserve
RBWC rates in real terms against monthly fluctuations in its input costs, due to
changes in inflation, foreign exchange rate movements and changes in electricity
rates.
3.3. The mathematical computation of the PAM is as follows:
PAM = (w *ΔFX + w *ΔCPI + w *ΔkWh)*100
fx cpi kWh
Where:
ΔFX is the monthly percentage change in the J$/US$ exchange rate,
ΔCPI is the monthly percentage change in the CPI,
ΔkWh is the monthly percentage change in the kilowatt hour charge for
electricity,
w is the approved weight for the J$/US$ exchange rate,
fx
w is the approved weight for the CPI, and
cpi
w is the approved weight for the kilowatt hour charge for electricity.
kWh
3.4. The ANPAM normally allows for an adjustment of base rates and charges each year.
This is achieved by the ‘rolling- in’ of the cumulative PAM rate, from the time of last
ANPAM adjustment, into the base rates. The calculated ANPAM rate reflects the
weighted change in the base values, since the last ANPAM adjustment, for the three
(3) components in the mechanism.
3.5. Mathematically, the new base rates may be expressed as follows:
New Base Rate = Current Base Rate * (1 + ANPAM adjustment rate).
3.6. In keeping with the Office’s decision to apply an ANPAM rate equivalent to that of
the NWC to the RBWC, the OUR verified the proposed 3.62% ANPAM against the
ANPAM rate that was approved for the NWC.
3.7. The sources of the input data for the ANPAM granted to NWC are as follows:
1. Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN) for Consumer Price Index (CPI)
2. Bank of Jamaica (BOJ) for foreign exchange (FX) rate (J$:US$); and

3.9. On 2025 April 28, the Office issued the National Water Commission Annual Price
Adjustment Mechanism 2025 Rate Adjustment Determination Notice, document
number 2025/WAS/006/DET.001 in which it approved the ANPAM rate adjustment
of 3.62%. The ANPAM rate adjustment was applied to bills issued by the Commission
in 2025 May for services rendered in the month of 2025 April.
3.10. Considering the OUR’s decision to align RBWC’s ANPAM with that of the NWC, it
implies that the approved ANPAM rate adjustment of 3.62% for the NWC is now
applicable to RBWC. Accordingly, in keeping with the Determination Notice, the
current baseline rates as shown in Table 3.1 above, shall be adjusted to reflect the
new baseline parameters of FX: $158.11, CPI: 141.80 and Electricity: $50.59/kWh.
This translates to the base rates adjustment of 3.62%.
3.11. No proposal was received for an adjustment to the company’s
miscellaneous/reconnection fees.
3.12. In its application RBWC submitted a proposed rate schedule, which inadvertently
included its 2023 base rates instead of its 2024 base rates, on which the 3.62%
adjustment rate is to be applied. The OUR recognised the error and applied the
adjustment rate of 3.62% to the 2024 base rates which were approved in the RBWC
ANPAM Determination Notice 2024 document number 2024/WAS/010/DET.004
dated 2024 July 24.
3.13. The new base rates and charges for RBWC are displayed in Table 3.2 below. The new
rates will become effective on customers’ 2025 June bills.

Determination 1
1. The Office approves the ANPAM rate adjustment of 3.62%, which
shall apply to RBWC’s base rates and charges.
2. The application of the ANPAM rate adjustment is effective on
customers’ 2025 June bills.
3. Miscellaneous/reconnection fee remains unchanged.
4. RBWC new base rates will remain in effect until the next programmed
reset of the ANPAM or the implementation of new tariffs, whichever
is earlier.
